business_objectives: Provide a secure, scalable multi-tenant platform that centralizes hospital operations, improves patient care, streamlines appointment and clinical workflows, enables efficient administration, integrates with external healthcare services, delivers real-time analytics and reporting, reduces operational costs, and supports future expansion such as telemedicine and AI-powered healthcare services.

answers.answer: Provide a secure, scalable multi-tenant platform that centralizes hospital operations, improves patient care, streamlines appointment and clinical workflows, enables efficient administration, integrates with external healthcare services, delivers real-time analytics and reporting, reduces operational costs, and supports future expansion such as telemedicine and AI-powered healthcare services.

The initial release should include patient registration and login, role-based authentication, appointment booking, rescheduling and cancellation, doctor appointment management, electronic medical records, diagnosis and prescription management, laboratory test requests and report uploads, pharmacy inventory and medicine dispensing, billing and insurance verification, user and department management, notifications (SMS/email) for appointments, dashboards and basic reports, audit logging, and integration with payment gateways and notification services.

The system should support standardized clinical workflows. During patient check-in, staff should verify patient identity, insurance, and appointment details, update demographics if required, assign the patient to the appropriate department or doctor, and notify the assigned clinician. During emergency admission, the system should immediately register the patient with minimal mandatory information, assign a priority based on triage level, notify the emergency care team, allocate beds and required resources, and allow patient records to be completed after stabilization. During discharge, doctors should finalize diagnoses, prescriptions, and discharge summaries, billing should be completed, insurance claims processed if applicable, follow-up appointments scheduled, discharge documents generated, and all clinical and administrative actions recorded in the audit log.

The primary actors are Patients, Doctors, Nurses, Receptionists, Hospital Administrators, Laboratory Technicians, Pharmacists, Billing Staff, Insurance Coordinators, System Administrators, and external systems including Payment Gateways, SMS/Email Notification Services, Laboratory Devices, and Third-Party Insurance Providers.
